newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money edges up to 11.0/12.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money edges up to 11.0/12.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money edged up to 11.0/12.0 percent from 9.0/10.0 percent on Friday morning despite stable liquidity supply, dealers said.
They said the market was well supplied but rises of swap rates had driven overnight money higher.
Overnight swap was at 1.2/1.3 and tom/next at 0.60/0.64.
But longer-term rates were little changed from Thursday.
One-week money was at 12.75/13.00 and one-month money at 14.00/14.25 percent, brokers said.
Dealers said market focus was on liquidity conditions in the coming week due to the public offering of PT Bank Negara Indonesia shares from November 4-7.
They were generally confident that liquidity would remain stable because the market would not dry up as long as the money is not immediately transferred from the underwriters to the issuer BNI.
The average overnight interbank rate on Thursday was 9.11 percent, compared with 9.09 percent on Wednesday.
